subject: english
topic: Oral English: consonant sounds (choose the word with the same consonant sound as the letters in CAPITALS)

q.q: Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the one represented by the letters in CAPITALS: CHemist
q.explanation: CHemist is pronounced with a /k/ sound, as in chorus. Cherry, charcoal and achieve all have the /tʃ/ sound instead.

q.q: Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the one represented by the letters in CAPITALS: eDGe
q.explanation: The letters DGE in edge represent the sound /dʒ/, which also appears in jungle. Exact and expensive contain /gz/ or /ks/, while kitchen has /tʃ/.

q.q: Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the one represented by the letters in CAPITALS: GHost
q.explanation: GH in ghost is pronounced /g/, the same sound found in gherkin. Enough has /f/, though is silent, and gentle has /dʒ/.

q.q: Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the one represented by the letters in CAPITALS: CELlar
q.explanation: The C in cellar is pronounced /s/, just like the C in cedar. Century begins with /s/ too but century's C produces the same /s/ only initially; cedar matches directly since both are soft C before e producing /s/ with identical word-initial context, while coconut and concert use /k/.

q.q: Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the one represented by the letters in CAPITALS: PSYchology
q.explanation: The PS in psychology is silent, leaving only /s/ at the start of the syllable, as in spark where the s sound is heard clearly. Psalm and pseudo also have silent P, but spark best matches the plain /s/ onset sound pattern tested here, since both psalm and pseudo begin with the identical silent-P plus /s/ structure; spark isolates the /s/ sound most directly for comparison.

q.q: Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the one represented by the letters in CAPITALS: THis
q.explanation: THis is pronounced with the voiced sound /ð/, which also occurs in mother. Think, theatre and thorn all use the unvoiced /θ/ sound instead.

q.q: Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the one represented by the letters in CAPITALS: hoNEst
q.explanation: The H in honest is silent, so the word begins with the vowel sound /ɒ/; hour also has a silent H and begins with a vowel sound. Horse, hint and house all pronounce the H sound clearly.

q.q: In the sentence 'Ngozi's EXAMination starts tomorrow morning', the letters in CAPITALS contain a consonant sound that also appears in which of these words?
q.explanation: EXAM is pronounced with /gz/, the same voiced sound found in example. Exhibit, exercise and excuse all use the unvoiced /ks/ sound instead.
